fields.name: Protocol Version
fields.notes: See protocol version numbers (currently 777 in Minecraft 26.3).

fields.name: Server Address
fields.notes: Hostname or IP, e.g. localhost or 127.0.0.1, that was used to connect. The vanilla server does not use this information. This is the name obtained after SRV record resolution, except in 1.17 (and no older or newer version) and during server list ping (MC-278651), where it is the host portion of the address specified by the user directly. In 1.17.1 and later if a literal IP address is specified by the user, reverse DNS lookup is attempted, and the result is used as the value of this field if successful.

fields.name: Server Port
fields.notes: Default is 25565. The vanilla server does not use this information.

fields.name: Intent
fields.notes: 1 for Status, 2 for Login, 3 for Transfer. Intents 2 and 3 both transition to the Login state, but 3 indicates that the client is connecting due to a Transfer packet received from another server. If the server is not expecting transfers, it may choose to reject the connection by replying with a Disconnect (login) packet.

fields.name: JSON Response
fields.notes: See Java Edition protocol/Server List Ping#Status Response; as with all strings, this is prefixed by its length as a VarInt.

fields.name: Timestamp
fields.notes: Should match the one sent by the client.

fields.name: Timestamp
fields.notes: May be any number, but vanilla clients will always use the timestamp in milliseconds.

fields.name: Reason
fields.notes: The reason why the player was disconnected.

fields.name: Server ID
fields.notes: Always empty when sent by the vanilla server.

fields.name: Public Key
fields.notes: The server's public key, in bytes.

fields.name: Verify Token
fields.notes: A sequence of random bytes generated by the server.

fields.name: Should authenticate
fields.notes: Whether the client should attempt to authenticate through mojang servers.

fields.name: Threshold
fields.notes: Maximum size of a packet before it is compressed.

fields.name: Message ID
fields.notes: Generated by the server - should be unique to the connection.

fields.name: Channel
fields.notes: Name of the plugin channel used to send the data.

fields.name: Data
fields.notes: Any data, depending on the channel. Typically this would be a sequence of fields using standard data types, but some unofficial channels have unusual formats. There is no length prefix that applies to all channel types, but the format specific to the channel may or may not include one or more length prefixes (e.g. for strings). The vanilla client enforces a length limit of 1048576 bytes on this data, but only if the channel type is unrecognized (which is the case for all login plugin messages with a completely vanilla client).

fields.name: Key
fields.notes: The identifier of the cookie.

fields.name: Name
fields.notes: Player's Username.

fields.name: Player UUID
fields.notes: The UUID of the player logging in. Unused by the vanilla server.

fields.name: Shared Secret
fields.notes: Shared Secret value, encrypted with the server's public key.

fields.name: Verify Token
fields.notes: Verify Token value, encrypted with the same public key as the shared secret.

fields.name: Message ID
fields.notes: Should match ID from server.

fields.name: Data
fields.notes: Any data, depending on the channel. Only present if the client understood the request. Typically this would be a sequence of fields using standard data types, but some unofficial channels have unusual formats. There is no length prefix that applies to all channel types, but the format specific to the channel may or may not include one or more length prefixes (e.g. for strings).

fields.name: Key
fields.notes: The identifier of the cookie.

fields.type: Prefixed Optional Prefixed Array (5120) of Byte
fields.notes: The data of the cookie.

fields.name: UUID
fields.notes: The unique identifier of the resource pack.

fields.name: URL
fields.notes: The URL to the resource pack.

fields.name: Hash
fields.notes: A 40 character hexadecimal, case-insensitive SHA-1 hash of the resource pack file.If it's not a 40-character hexadecimal string, the client will not use it for hash verification and likely waste bandwidth.

fields.name: Forced
fields.notes: The vanilla client will be forced to use the resource pack from the server. If they decline, they will be kicked from the server.

fields.name: Prompt Message
fields.notes: This is shown in the prompt making the client accept or decline the resource pack (only if present).

fields.name: Post Effects
fields.notes: Identifiers of the post-processing effects to activate.

fields.name: Key

fields.name: Payload

fields.name: Host

fields.name: Port

fields.name: Known Packs
fields.notes: Namespace part of the name of the pack, such as minecraft.

elements.notes: Namespace part of the name of the pack, such as minecraft.

elements.name: ID
elements.notes: Pathname part of the name of the pack, such as core.

elements.name: Version
elements.notes: Version of the pack. For minecraft:core this corresponds to Minecraft version numbers, such as 1.21.10. Note that the vanilla data pack can change without a protocol version bump, and even a completely vanilla server talking to a vanilla client may fall back to sending all registry data over the wire, if the two are on different protocol-compatible patch versions.

fields.name: Links
fields.notes: Enums are used for built-in labels (see below), and text components for custom labels.

fields.name: Locale

fields.name: View Distance
fields.notes: Client-side render distance, in chunks.

fields.name: Chat Mode
fields.notes: 0: enabled, 1: commands only, 2: hidden. See Java Edition protocol/Chat#Client chat mode for more information.

fields.name: Chat Colors
fields.notes: “Colors” multiplayer setting. The vanilla server stores this value but does nothing with it (see ). Some third-party servers disable all coloring in chat and system messages when it is false.

fields.name: Displayed Skin Parts
fields.notes: Bit mask, see below.

fields.name: Main Hand
fields.notes: 0: Left, 1: Right.

fields.name: Enable text filtering
fields.notes: Enables filtering of text on signs and written book titles. The vanilla client sets this according to the profanityFilterPreferences.profanityFilterOn account attribute indicated by the Mojang API endpoint for player attributes. In offline mode, it is always false.

fields.name: Allow server listings
fields.notes: Servers usually list online players; this option should let you not show up in that list.

fields.name: Particle Status
fields.notes: 0: all, 1: decreased, 2: minimal

fields.name: ID
fields.notes: The identifier for the click action.

fields.name: Payload size
fields.notes: The number of bytes in the payload

fields.name: Payload
fields.notes: The data to send with the click action. May be a TAG_END (0).

fields.name: Entity ID
fields.notes: A unique integer ID mostly used in the protocol to identify the entity. If an entity with the same ID already exists on the client, it is automatically deleted and replaced by the new entity. On the vanilla server entity IDs are globally unique across all dimensions and never reused while the server is running, but not preserved across server restarts.

fields.name: Entity UUID
fields.notes: A unique identifier that is mostly used in persistence and places where the uniqueness matters more. It is possible to create multiple entities with the same UUID on the vanilla client, but a warning will be logged, and functionality dependent on UUIDs may ignore the entity or otherwise misbehave.

fields.name: Type
fields.notes: ID in the minecraft:entity_type registry (see "type" field in Java Edition protocol/Entity metadata#Entities).

fields.name: Head Yaw
fields.notes: Only used by living entities, where the head of the entity may differ from the general body rotation.

fields.name: Data
fields.notes: Meaning dependent on the value of the Type field, see Java Edition protocol/Object data for details.

fields.name: Entity ID
fields.notes: Entity ID.

fields.name: Animation
fields.notes: Animation ID (see below).

fields.name: Statistics

elements.notes: ID in the minecraft:stat_type registry; see below.

elements.name: Statistic ID
elements.notes: See below.

elements.name: Value
elements.notes: The amount to set it to.

fields.name: Sequence ID
fields.notes: Represents the sequence to acknowledge; this is used for properly syncing block changes to the client after interactions.

fields.name: Entity ID
fields.notes: The ID of the entity breaking the block.

fields.name: Location

fields.name: Destroy Stage

fields.name: Type
fields.notes: ID in the minecraft:block_entity_type registry

fields.name: NBT Data
fields.notes: Data to set.

fields.name: Action Parameter (Byte 2)
fields.notes: Varies depending on block — see Java Edition protocol/Block actions.

fields.name: Block Type
fields.notes: ID in the minecraft:block registry. This value is unused by the vanilla client, as it will infer the type of block based on the given position.

fields.name: Location

fields.name: Block ID
fields.notes: The new block state ID for the block as given in the global block state palette.

fields.name: UUID

elements.name: Flags

fields.notes: This is the ID of the window that was closed. 0 for inventory.

fields.name: Window ID
fields.notes: The ID of window which items are being sent for. 0 for player inventory. The client ignores any packets targeting a Window ID other than the current one. However, an exception is made for the player inventory, which may be targeted at any time. (The vanilla server does not appear to utilize this special case.)

fields.name: Window ID
fields.notes: The window that is being updated. 0 for player inventory. The client ignores any packets targeting a Window ID other than the current one; see below for exceptions.

fields.name: State ID

fields.name: Slot
fields.notes: The slot that should be updated.

fields.notes: Number of ticks to apply a cooldown for, or 0 to clear the cooldown.

fields.name: Source Position

fields.name: Message ID
fields.notes: The message ID + 1, used for validating message signature. The next field is present only when value of this field is equal to 0.

fields.name: Signature
fields.notes: The previous message's signature. Always 256 bytes and not length-prefixed.

fields.name: Reason
fields.notes: The reason why the player was disconnected.

fields.name: Message
fields.notes: This is used as the content parameter when formatting the message on the client.

fields.name: Target Name

fields.name: Entity ID
fields.notes: The "owner" entity of the GUI. The client should close the GUI if the owner entity dies or is cleared.

fields.name: Entity ID

fields.name: Yaw

fields.name: New Diameter
fields.notes: Target length of a single side of the world border, in meters.

fields.name: Speed
fields.notes: Number of real-time milliseconds until New Diameter is reached. It appears that vanilla server does not sync world border speed to game ticks, so it gets out of sync with server lag. If the world border is not moving, this is set to 0.

fields.name: Portal Teleport Boundary
fields.notes: Resulting coordinates from a portal teleport are limited to ±value. Usually 29999984.

fields.name: Warning Blocks
fields.notes: In meters.

fields.name: Warning Time
fields.notes: In seconds as set by /worldborder warning time.

fields.notes: Chunk coordinate (block coordinate divided by 16, rounded down)

elements.name: Type

fields.name: View Distance

fields.name: Simulation Distance
fields.notes: Server simulation distance. See Set Simulation Distance.

fields.notes: If true, a vanilla client shows reduced information on the debug screen. For servers in development, this should almost always be false.

fields.name: Enable respawn screen
fields.notes: Set to false when the doImmediateRespawn gamerule is true.

fields.name: Do limited crafting
fields.notes: Whether players can only craft recipes they have already unlocked. Currently unused by the client.

fields.name: Dimension Type
fields.notes: The ID of the type of dimension in the minecraft:dimension_type registry, defined by the Registry Data packet.

fields.name: Dimension Name
fields.notes: Name of the dimension being spawned into.

fields.name: Hashed seed
fields.notes: First 8 bytes of the SHA-256 hash of the world's seed. Used client-side for biome noise

fields.name: Game mode
fields.notes: 0: Survival, 1: Creative, 2: Adventure, 3: Spectator.

fields.name: Previous Game mode
fields.notes: Optional game mode encoding: 0 means undefined; otherwise the value is the game mode ID plus 1 (1: Survival, 2: Creative, 3: Adventure, 4: Spectator). Vanilla client uses this for the debug (F3 + N & F3 + F4) game mode switch.

fields.name: Is Debug
fields.notes: True if the world is a debug mode world; debug mode worlds cannot be modified and have predefined blocks.

fields.name: Is Flat
fields.notes: True if the world is a superflat world; flat worlds have different void fog and a horizon at Y=0 instead of Y=63.

fields.name: Has death location
fields.notes: If true, then the next two fields are present.

fields.name: Death dimension name
fields.notes: Name of the dimension the player died in.

fields.name: Death location
fields.notes: The location that the player died at.

fields.name: Portal cooldown
fields.notes: The number of ticks until the player can use the last used portal again. Looks like it's an attempt to fix MC-180.

fields.name: Map ID
fields.notes: Map ID of the map being modified

fields.name: Scale
fields.notes: From 0 for a fully zoomed-in map (1 block per pixel) to 4 for a fully zoomed-out map (16 blocks per pixel)

fields.name: Locked
fields.notes: True if the map has been locked in a cartography table

fields.name: Trades
fields.notes: See below. The first item the player has to supply for this villager trade. The count of the item stack is the default "price" of this trade.

elements.name: Input item 1
elements.notes: See below. The first item the player has to supply for this villager trade. The count of the item stack is the default "price" of this trade.

elements.name: Output item
elements.notes: The item the player will receive from this villager trade.

elements.name: Input item 2
elements.notes: The second item the player has to supply for this villager trade.

elements.name: Trade disabled
elements.notes: True if the trade is disabled; false if the trade is enabled.

elements.name: Number of trade uses
elements.notes: Number of times the trade has been used so far. If equal to the maximum number of trades, the client will display a red X.

elements.name: Maximum number of trade uses
elements.notes: Number of times this trade can be used before it's exhausted.

elements.name: XP
elements.notes: Amount of XP the villager will earn each time the trade is used.

elements.name: Special Price
elements.notes: Can be zero or negative. The number is added to the price when an item is discounted due to player reputation or other effects.

elements.notes: The name of the argument that is signed by the following signature.

elements.name: Signature
elements.notes: The signature that verifies the argument. Always 256 bytes and is not length-prefixed.

fields.name: Message
fields.notes: Content of the message

fields.name: Timestamp
fields.notes: Number of milliseconds since the epoch (1 Jan 1970, midnight, UTC)

fields.name: Salt
fields.notes: The salt used to verify the signature hash. Randomly generated by the client

fields.name: Signature
fields.notes: The signature used to verify the chat message's authentication. When present, always 256 bytes and not length-prefixed.

fields.name: Message Count
fields.notes: Number of signed clientbound chat messages the client has seen from the server since the last serverbound chat message from this client. The server will use this to update its last seen list for the client.

fields.name: Acknowledged
fields.notes: Bitmask of which message signatures from the last seen set were used to sign this message. The most recent is the highest bit. If there are fewer than 20 messages in the last seen set, the lower bits will be zeros.

fields.name: Checksum
fields.notes: Checksum is computed over all the message signature checksums in the last seen set, from oldest to newest. Both the packet checksum and signature checksums use the same logic as Java's Arrays.hashCode(byte[]) implementation. The packet checksum additionally casts the resulting int to a byte, and if that byte is 0 returns 1, otherwise returns said byte

fields.name: Public Key
fields.notes: The time the play session key expires in milliseconds.

elements.name: Expires At
elements.notes: The time the play session key expires in milliseconds.

elements.name: Public Key
elements.notes: A byte array of an X.509-encoded public key. Get this from Mojang API#Get keypair for signature

elements.name: Key Signature
elements.notes: The signature consists of the player UUID, the key expiration timestamp, and the public key data. These values are hashed using and signed using Mojang's private key.

fields.name: Chunks per tick
fields.notes: Desired chunks per tick.

fields.name: Action ID
fields.notes: See below

fields.name: Locale
fields.notes: e.g. en_GB.

fields.name: View Distance
fields.notes: Client-side render distance, in chunks.

fields.name: Chat Mode
fields.notes: 0: enabled, 1: commands only, 2: hidden. See Java Edition protocol/Chat#Client chat mode for more information.

fields.name: Chat Colors
fields.notes: “Colors” multiplayer setting. The vanilla server stores this value but does nothing with it (see ). Some third-party servers disable all coloring in chat and system messages when it is false.

fields.name: Displayed Skin Parts
fields.notes: Bit mask, see below.

fields.name: Main Hand
fields.notes: 0: Left, 1: Right.

fields.name: Enable text filtering
fields.notes: Enables filtering of text on signs and written book titles. The vanilla client sets this according to the profanityFilterPreferences.profanityFilterOn account attribute indicated by the Mojang API endpoint for player attributes. In offline mode, it is always false.

fields.name: Allow server listings
fields.notes: Servers usually list online players; this option should let you not show up in that list.

fields.name: Particle Status
fields.notes: 0: all, 1: decreased, 2: minimal

fields.name: Transaction Id
fields.notes: The ID of the transaction that the server will send back to the client in the response of this packet. Client generates this and increments it each time it sends another tab completion that doesn't get a response.

fields.name: Text
fields.notes: All the text behind the cursor including the / (e.g. to the left of the cursor in left-to-right languages like English).

fields.name: Window ID
fields.notes: The ID of the window sent by Open Screen.

fields.name: Button ID
fields.notes: Meaning depends on window type; see below.

fields.name: Window ID
fields.notes: The ID of the window that was clicked. 0 for player inventory. The server ignores any packets targeting a Window ID other than the current one, including ignoring 0 when any other window is open.

fields.name: State ID
fields.notes: The last received State ID from either a Set Container Slot or a Set Container Content packet.

fields.name: Slot
fields.notes: The clicked slot number, see below.

fields.name: Button
fields.notes: The button used in the click, see below.

fields.name: Mode
fields.notes: Inventory operation mode, see below.

elements.name: Slot data
elements.notes: New data for this slot, in the client's opinion; see below.

fields.name: Carried item
fields.notes: Item carried by the cursor.

fields.name: Window ID
fields.notes: This is the ID of the window that was closed. 0 for player inventory.

fields.name: Slot ID
fields.notes: This is the ID of the slot that was changed.

fields.name: Window ID
fields.notes: This is the ID of the window that was changed.

fields.name: State
fields.notes: The new state of the slot. True for enabled, false for disabled.

fields.name: Key
fields.notes: The identifier of the cookie.

fields.name: Payload
fields.type: Prefixed Optional Prefixed Array (5120) of Byte
fields.notes: The data of the cookie.

fields.name: Channel
fields.notes: Name of the plugin channel used to send the data.

fields.name: Data
fields.notes: Any data, depending on the channel. Typically this would be a sequence of fields using standard data types, but some unofficial channels have unusual formats. There is no length prefix that applies to all channel types, but the format specific to the channel may or may not include one or more length prefixes (such as the string length prefix in the standard minecraft:brand channel). The vanilla server enforces a length limit of 32767 bytes on this data, but only if the channel type is unrecognized.

fields.name: Subscriptions
fields.notes: List of active debug subscriptions. IDs in the minecraft:debug_subscription registry.

fields.name: Slot
fields.notes: The hotbar slot where the written book is located

fields.name: Entries
fields.notes: Text from each page. Maximum string length is 1024 chars.

fields.name: Title
fields.notes: Title of book. Present if book is being signed, not present if book is being edited.

fields.name: Transaction ID
fields.notes: An incremental ID so that the client can verify that the response matches.

fields.name: Entity ID
fields.notes: The ID of the entity to query.

fields.name: Entity ID
fields.notes: The ID of the entity to interact. Note the special case described below.

fields.name: Hand
fields.notes: Only if Type is interact or interact at; 0: main hand, 1: off hand.

fields.name: Sneak Key Pressed
fields.notes: If the client is pressing the sneak key. Has the same effect as a Player Command Press/Release sneak key preceding the interaction, and the state is permanently changed.

fields.name: Location
fields.notes: Block entity location.

fields.name: Levels
fields.notes: Value of the levels slider/max depth to generate.

fields.name: X
fields.notes: Absolute position.

fields.name: Feet Y
fields.notes: Absolute feet position, normally Head Y - 1.62.

fields.name: Z
fields.notes: Absolute position.

fields.name: Flags
fields.notes: Bit field: 0x01: on ground, 0x02: pushing against wall.

fields.name: X
fields.notes: Absolute position.

fields.name: Feet Y
fields.notes: Absolute feet position, normally Head Y - 1.62.

fields.name: Z
fields.notes: Absolute position.

fields.name: Yaw
fields.notes: Absolute rotation on the X Axis, in degrees.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.notes: Absolute rotation on the Y Axis, in degrees.

fields.name: Flags
fields.notes: Bit field: 0x01: on ground, 0x02: pushing against wall.

fields.name: Yaw
fields.notes: Absolute rotation on the X Axis, in degrees.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.notes: Absolute rotation on the Y Axis, in degrees.

fields.name: Flags
fields.notes: Bit field: 0x01: on ground, 0x02: pushing against wall.

fields.name: Flags
fields.notes: Bit field: 0x01: on ground, 0x02: pushing against wall.

fields.name: X
fields.notes: Absolute position (X coordinate).

fields.name: Y
fields.notes: Absolute position (Y coordinate).

fields.name: Z
fields.notes: Absolute position (Z coordinate).

fields.name: Yaw
fields.notes: Absolute rotation on the vertical axis, in degrees.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.notes: Absolute rotation on the horizontal axis, in degrees.

fields.name: On Ground
fields.notes: Whether the vehicle is on the ground.

fields.name: Location
fields.notes: The location of the block.

fields.name: Include Data
fields.notes: Used to tell the server to include block data in the new stack, works only if in creative mode.

fields.name: Entity ID
fields.notes: The ID of the entity to pick.

fields.name: Include Data
fields.notes: Unused by the vanilla server.

fields.name: Recipe ID
fields.notes: ID of recipe previously defined in Recipe Book Add.

fields.name: Make all
fields.notes: Affects the amount of items processed; true if shift is down when clicked.

fields.name: Flags
fields.notes: Bit mask. 0x02: is flying.

fields.name: Status
fields.notes: The action the player is taking against the block (see below).

fields.name: Location
fields.notes: Block position.

fields.name: Face
fields.notes: The face being hit (see below).

fields.name: Sequence
fields.notes: Block change sequence number (see #Acknowledge Block Change).

fields.name: Entity ID
fields.notes: Player ID (ignored by the vanilla server)

fields.name: Action ID
fields.notes: The ID of the action, see below.

fields.name: Jump Boost
fields.notes: Only used by the “start jump with horse” action, in which case it ranges from 0 to 100. In all other cases it is 0.

fields.name: Flags
fields.notes: Bit mask; see below

fields.name: Book ID
fields.notes: 0: crafting, 1: furnace, 2: blast furnace, 3: smoker.

fields.name: Recipe ID
fields.notes: ID of recipe previously defined in Recipe Book Add.

fields.name: Item name
fields.notes: The new name of the item.

fields.name: UUID
fields.notes: The unique identifier of the resource pack received in the Add Resource Pack request.

fields.name: Result
fields.notes: Result ID (see below).

fields.name: Tab ID
fields.notes: Only present if action is Opened tab.

fields.name: Selected slot
fields.notes: The selected slot in the player's current (trading) inventory.

fields.name: Primary Effect
fields.notes: A Potion ID.

fields.name: Secondary Effect
fields.notes: A Potion ID.

fields.name: Slot
fields.notes: The slot which the player has selected (0–8).

fields.name: Mode
fields.notes: 0: chain, 1: repeating, 2: impulse.

fields.name: Flags
fields.notes: 0x01: Track Output (if false, the output of the previous command will not be stored within the command block); 0x02: Is conditional; 0x04: Automatic.

fields.name: Track Output
fields.notes: If false, the output of the previous command will not be stored within the command block.

fields.name: Slot
fields.notes: Inventory slot.

fields.name: Location
fields.notes: Block entity location

fields.name: Final state
fields.notes: "Turns into" on the GUI, final_state in NBT.

fields.name: Joint type
fields.notes: rollable if the attached piece can be rotated, else aligned.

fields.name: Location
fields.notes: Block entity location.

fields.name: Mode
fields.notes: One of SAVE (0), LOAD (1), CORNER (2), DATA (3).

fields.name: Mirror
fields.notes: One of NONE (0), LEFT_RIGHT (1), FRONT_BACK (2).

fields.name: Rotation
fields.notes: One of NONE (0), CLOCKWISE_90 (1), CLOCKWISE_180 (2), COUNTERCLOCKWISE_90 (3).

fields.name: Integrity
fields.notes: Between 0 and 1.

fields.name: Flags
fields.notes: 0x01: Ignore entities; 0x02: Show air; 0x04: Show bounding box; 0x08: Strict placement.

fields.name: Mode
fields.notes: 0: start, 1: log, 2: fail, 3: accept

fields.name: Location
fields.notes: Block coordinates.

fields.name: Line 1
fields.notes: First line of text in the sign.

fields.name: Line 2
fields.notes: Second line of text in the sign.

fields.name: Line 3
fields.notes: Third line of text in the sign.

fields.name: Line 4
fields.notes: Fourth line of text in the sign.

fields.name: Text Slot
fields.notes: Selects which sign text slot is updated; see below.

fields.name: Entity ID
fields.notes: If 0, the player was not targeting an entity. Otherwise the ID of the targeted entity plus 1.

fields.name: Target Player
fields.notes: UUID of the player to teleport to (can also be an entity UUID).

fields.name: Test
fields.notes: ID in the minecraft:test_instance registry.

fields.name: Rotation
fields.notes: 0: none, 1: clockwise 90°, 2: clockwise 180°, 3: counter-clockwise 90°.

fields.name: Status
fields.notes: 0: cleared, 1: running, 2: finished.

fields.name: Hand
fields.notes: The hand from which the block is placed; 0: main hand, 1: off hand.

fields.name: Location
fields.notes: Block position.

fields.name: Face
fields.notes: The face on which the block is placed (as documented at Player Action).

fields.name: Cursor Position X
fields.notes: The position of the crosshair on the block, from 0 to 1 increasing from west to east.

fields.name: Cursor Position Y
fields.notes: The position of the crosshair on the block, from 0 to 1 increasing from bottom to top.

fields.name: Cursor Position Z
fields.notes: The position of the crosshair on the block, from 0 to 1 increasing from north to south.

fields.name: Inside block
fields.notes: True when the player's head is inside of a block.

fields.name: World Border Hit
fields.notes: Seems to always be false, even when interacting with blocks around or outside the world border, or while the player is outside the border.

fields.name: Sequence
fields.notes: Block change sequence number (see #Acknowledge Block Change).

fields.name: Hand
fields.notes: Hand used for the animation. 0: main hand, 1: off hand.

fields.name: Sequence
fields.notes: Block change sequence number (see #Acknowledge Block Change).

fields.name: Yaw
fields.notes: Player head rotation around the Y-Axis.

fields.name: Pitch
fields.notes: Player head rotation around the X-Axis.

fields.name: ID
fields.notes: The identifier for the click action.

fields.name: Payload size
fields.notes: The number of bytes in the payload

fields.name: Payload
fields.notes: The data to send with the click action. May be a TAG_END (0).
